summary.motive: Vertically stretch one flat defender with three routes at three depths until he must give up a leg of the flood.
summary.whyItWorks: The seam threat removes the hook linebacker and the deep third holds the safety high, leaving the corner alone to cover both an inside breaker and a flat runner.
summary.failureMode: The Sam refuses to carry the TE vertical and walls the curl while the corner takes the flat, erasing all three windows.

beats.title: 1. The Three-Level Flood Forms
beats.text: To the right, three receivers attack three depths at once: the TE climbs past fifteen, the flanker works eight at the numbers, and the fullback swings into the flat.

beats.title: 2. The Seam Threat Drags the Hook
beats.text: The TE's vertical stem forces the Sam linebacker to carry him up the seam, vacating the very curl window the flood is designed to hit underneath.

beats.title: 3. The High-Low Question
beats.text: The quarterback reads the sky safety against the curl. The safety stays above the fifteen-yard break, so the curl window is open if the corner does not close it.

beats.title: 4. The Corner Loses the Flood
beats.text: The flat-drop corner sat on Z's inside break, and now the fullback runs free behind him in the flat. The quarterback throws down to the shallowest open leg.

relations.tell: All three flood legs release to one side within the first second — a true flood never distributes to both sides.
